demo.title: 5 tips to kick off your first project

content.intro: Starting your first upcycling project can seem intimidating. Here are the essential tips to get off on the right foot and avoid classic mistakes.
content.p1: Don't tackle a big antique wardrobe for your first project. Instead, choose something simple: a chair, a wooden crate, a small frame. You'll build confidence and skill before taking on more ambitious projects.
content.p2: A few essential tools are enough to get started: electric sander, screwdriver, hammer, tape measure, sandpaper (grits 80, 120, 220), brushes. Avoid overly cheap tools that will quickly discourage you.
content.p3: Work in a well-ventilated space with good lighting. Lay down a tarp. Wear appropriate PPE (personal protective equipment): goggles, mask, gloves.
content.p4: Take before/during/after photos. It's rewarding, it helps you improve, and it's perfect for sharing your work on the UpcycleConnect forum.
content.p5: Our community is here for you. Don't hesitate to post your questions on the forum — most questions get an answer within 24 hours.

seed.title: How do I turn an old pallet into a coffee table?
seed.content:
I picked up 3 construction pallets in good condition and I'd like to make a coffee table for my living room.

Questions:
- Should I sand the pallets before assembly?
- What finish for indoor use?
- How do I attach the casters?

Thanks in advance!

m1.content:
Hey Marie, great project!

1. Yes, sanding is essential: grit 80, 120, 220.
2. For indoor use, a hard oil like Rubio Monocoat.
3. 75mm swivel casters with lag bolts + embedded nuts.

m2.content: Watch out for treated pallets (HT marking = OK, MB = avoid for indoor use).

m3.content: Thanks to both of you! My pallets are properly marked HT
